clue.text: Time for a pop festival?

parts.note: pop is a familiar word for a dad, so a festival for pops is the yearly day in June that honours fathers

explanation.surface: Someone asks when the summer pop music festival is on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' suggests pop music; here it means a father, and the 'festival' is the annual day set aside for fathers.
explanation.definitionFit: The day each June when children honour their dads is a celebration of 'pops', a family festival.

clue.text: What pacifists have, but do not use

definitions.text: What pacifists have, but do not use

indicators.note: the word pacifists has these letters within it, so having signals the hidden run

explanation.surface: Pacifists possess something they refuse to put to use.
explanation.walkthrough: Pacifists have clenched hands like anyone, but will not fight; the word 'pacifists' also holds the answer as its last five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Clenched hands are what a peace-lover owns but never strikes with, and the word sits in its own last letters.

clue.text: The fiscal system makes allowances for them

definitions.text: The fiscal system makes allowances for them

parts.words: The fiscal system makes allowances for them
parts.note: making allowances means being lenient, but in tax law allowances are sums one may earn free of tax

explanation.surface: The financial system is forgiving towards certain people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes allowances' sounds like tolerance; in Britain personal allowances are amounts of income exempt from tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who owe the Revenue money are granted personal allowances, tax-free slices of income.

clue.text: Time to steer a different way

indicators.note: steering a different way means the letters are taken in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: It is time to change course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different way' rearranges the letters of STEER and A.
explanation.definitionFit: The spring festival of the Resurrection is a season, a time of the Christian year.

clue.text: Islanders put northern Scot in ancient city

indicators.note: the northern Scot is put inside the city's name, so in signals containment

parts.note: Sardis was the ancient capital of Lydia in Asia Minor
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: Islanders have placed a northern Scotsman in an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put ... in' signals the container. Sardis, capital of ancient Lydia, is the city; 'Scot' looks like a nationality but stands for a typical Scottish first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives of Sardinia, the large Italian island west of Italy, are islanders.

clue.text: Instances of over'cad music?

parts.note: the smudged word is overhead: music overhead is music in the sky, and tunes are known by a word that names the atmosphere

explanation.surface: Examples of music played above one's head.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'over'cad'; the clue means 'overhead'. Tunes are called by the same word as the atmosphere above us, so music overhead is literally in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Melodies or tunes share their name with the atmosphere, so music overhead is music up there.

clue.text: More than enough to give Tony a sinful look

definitions.text: to give Tony a sinful look
definitions.meaning: put these letters in front of the name Tony and you get the deadly sin of overeating

explanation.surface: Someone has been given more than enough, enough to make Tony look wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic instruction: the answer placed before TONY spells GLUTTONY, one of the seven deadly sins.
explanation.definitionFit: A surplus of goods on the market is called this; the word also starts the sin of greedy eating.

clue.text: A girl in danger conceals her identity

definitions.text: A girl in danger conceals her identity

indicators.note: the phrase girl in danger keeps the name tucked inside it, so concealing signals the hidden run

explanation.surface: A threatened young woman goes incognito.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conceals' signals a run spanning 'girL IN DAnger': the girl's identity, her name, is concealed in those words.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name is what identifies her, and this name lies across the words about her.

clue.text: A cosy sort of place where caddies provide refreshment

definitions.text: A cosy sort of place where caddies provide refreshment

parts.words: A cosy sort of place where caddies provide refreshment
parts.note: caddies suggest golf, but a caddy is also a tin for tea leaves, and a cosy keeps the pot warm, so this is an outdoor café

explanation.surface: A snug spot where golf caddies bring drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caddies' points to golf and 'cosy' to comfort; a tea caddy holds tea leaves and a tea cosy covers the pot.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-air café serving tea and cakes, the kind of place tea caddies and cosies belong.

clue.text: Togs are put into safe keeping

indicators.note: the letters are put into a fresh order to make the phrase for safe keeping

explanation.surface: Clothes are placed in safe keeping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put into' rearranges the seven letters of TOGS ARE; 'Togs' reads as clothes being stored, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping goods in a warehouse or cupboard until needed is safe keeping.

clue.text: Numbers of big hits

definitions.meaning: figures, here the number 6 in the plural
in cricket a hit clearing the boundary on the full scores six runs

explanation.surface: A tally of the big hits in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a ball hit over the boundary without bouncing scores six runs and is itself called a six.
explanation.definitionFit: Several of the figure 6 are counted as digits, and cricket names its biggest boundary strike after its score.

clue.text: Country that saw a pretender crowned. Hope he made it

definitions.text: Country that saw a pretender crowned. Hope he made it

parts.words: Country that saw a pretender crowned. Hope he made it
parts.note: Anthony Hope invented this imaginary kingdom for The Prisoner of Zenda, where a lookalike Englishman is crowned in the king's place

explanation.surface: A country crowned an impostor, and one hopes he got away with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hope he made it' reads as a wish; Hope is the novelist Anthony Hope, who made up the country in The Prisoner of Zenda (1894).
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional central European kingdom of Hope's novel, where an impostor stands in for the king at the coronation.

clue.text: No angel fish, this

parts.note: the opposite of an angel is a devil, and there is a marine fish named for one, set against the angelfish

explanation.surface: A remark that this fish is no angelfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No angel' sounds like a comment on behaviour; it points to the angel's opposite, the devil, which also names a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The anglerfish or devil ray is called by this hyphenated name, the fiendish counterpart of the angelfish.

clue.text: Equip a girl for Naval war service

parts.note: to arm is to equip with weapons
Ada is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Kitting out a young woman for wartime service in the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Equip a girl' reads as preparing a recruit, but it is two pieces: ARM and the name ADA.
explanation.definitionFit: A great fleet of warships sent to fight at sea, like the Spanish one of 1588.

clue.text: Do they shelve their responsibilities?

parts.note: shelving responsibilities means shirking them, but literally it means putting the books in one's care onto shelves

explanation.surface: A question about people who dodge their duties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shelve' usually means postpone or avoid; here it is literal, putting books on shelves, the job of those running a library.
explanation.definitionFit: Library staff literally put the books in their charge back on shelves, the duty of their post.

clue.text: A mirthful catch

parts.note: a catch is a round sung by several voices, and a cheerful part-song of that kind shares its name with merriment

explanation.surface: A good-humoured catch, perhaps in a ball game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch' suggests a ball held in the field; here it is the old sung round, and the answer is both merriment and an unaccompanied part-song.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means mirth and also names a short part-song for several voices, a relative of the catch.

clue.text: Sporting birds, in the main

parts.note: in the main reads as mostly, but a main is a match of cockfights, where fighting birds are set against each other

explanation.surface: Birds that are mostly used for sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' looks like 'on the whole'; a main is a series of matches in cockfighting, where these fighting birds compete.
explanation.definitionFit: Roosters bred for fighting are birds of sport, matched against each other in a main.

clue.text: Headgear for, a Yorkshire woman ?

parts.note: Yorkshire was divided into three Ridings, so a hood from there would be a ..., as worn by the fairy-tale girl in red

explanation.surface: Asking what hat a woman from Yorkshire might wear.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire was historically divided into three districts called Ridings; the hooded cloak recalls Little Red Riding Hood.
explanation.definitionFit: A hood worn for riding on horseback, the garment that gave the fairy-tale heroine her name.

clue.text: Harmonics are the obvious ones

parts.note: overt means open and obvious

explanation.surface: Harmonics are said to be the most noticeable notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harmonics' is the definition; the rest reads as a comment that harmonics are the most noticeable notes, but splits into a word for open plus 'ones' kept as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Higher notes sounding above a fundamental are the harmonics, also called upper partials.

clue.text: Poor Dad is in contempt

indicators.note: poor signals the letters are in bad shape and must be reorganised

explanation.surface: A badly-off father is being held in contempt of court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges the letters DADISIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorn or disdainful looking down on someone is contempt.

clue.text: So Mary is in trouble with' the Bishop's. cassowary ?

definitions.note: a comic rhyme attributed to Bishop Samuel Wilberforce has a cassowary on the plains of Timbuctoo eating a churchman abroad; the definition is the bird's meal

indicators.note: letters in trouble are thrown into disorder and come out rearranged

explanation.surface: Mary has got into difficulties with a bishop's pet cassowary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' rearranges SOMARYISIN. The verse runs 'If I were a cassowary on the plains of Timbuctoo, I would eat a missionary, cassock, band and hymn-book too'.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme's cassowary eats a preacher sent out to convert, so the bird's prey is a churchman abroad.

clue.text: The actor sounds enthusiastic

indicators.note: sounds signals that the word is identified by how it is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: keen means enthusiastic

explanation.surface: The actor comes across as eager.
explanation.walkthrough: Edmund Kean was the great English tragic actor of the early 1800s; his surname is pronounced like KEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Kean, the celebrated Shakespearean tragedian of Regency London, is the actor meant.

clue.text: " And spades, the of untimely graves " (Cowper)

definitions.text: " And spades, the of untimely graves " (Cowper)

parts.words: " And spades, the of untimely graves " (Cowper)
parts.note: a gap-fill from William Cowper's poem, where the playing-card suit of spades is called the symbol of early death

explanation.surface: A line of verse by Cowper about spades and early graves.
explanation.walkthrough: The missing word comes from Cowper's The Task, on card-playing: 'And spades, the emblem of untimely graves'; a spade digs a grave, so the suit symbolises it.
explanation.definitionFit: A symbol: Cowper calls the suit of spades the sign of early death, since spades dig graves.

clue.text: Chirpy little creature

parts.note: chirpy reads as cheerful, but here it is literal: an insect that makes a loud chirping noise

explanation.surface: A description of a cheerful small animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chirpy' usually means bright and lively; here it means producing a chirp, as this insect famously does in summer.
explanation.definitionFit: This insect is known for its shrill chirring song in hot weather, a small creature that literally chirps.

clue.text: One of many provided by W. W. Jacobs

definitions.text: One of many provided by W. W. Jacobs

parts.words: One of many provided by W. W. Jacobs
parts.note: W. W. Jacobs wrote a story collection called Many ..., so a single item is one of its title objects, a ship's load

explanation.surface: A single item among many supplied by the author W. W. Jacobs.
explanation.walkthrough: W. W. Jacobs, author of The Monkey's Paw, published the collection of seafaring tales Many Cargoes (1896).
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's load of goods; Jacobs titled his first book Many Cargoes.

clue.text: One who is more ready to help at any stage

definitions.meaning: prompt means ready and quick, so the comparative means more ready
in a theatre someone in the wings feeds forgotten lines to the actors on stage

explanation.surface: A person always readier than others to lend a hand at any point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At any stage' reads as 'at any time'; it means on a theatre stage, where this person cues actors who forget their lines.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the comparative of prompt (quicker, readier) and the theatre helper who cues actors.

clue.text: Birds on board

definitions.meaning: black crows that nest in colonies
chess pieces that move straight along ranks and files, also called castles

explanation.surface: Birds have got on board a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' sounds like being aboard a ship; it means on the chessboard, where the castles are also known by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The black birds of the crow family share their name with the castle pieces in chess.

clue.text: The figure of 101

parts.note: 101 is a hundred, Roman C, followed by one
the remaining unit of 101 is the number one spelt out

explanation.surface: Asking what shape the number 101 has.
explanation.walkthrough: '101' is split as C (the Roman numeral 100) and ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A geometric figure or solid with a round base tapering to a point, like an ice-cream holder.

clue.text: Eating with them might be a joint affair

definitions.text: Eating with them might be a joint affair

parts.words: Eating with them might be a joint affair
parts.note: a joint is a cut of roast meat, so for this order of flesh-eating mammals every meal involves meat, not sharing

explanation.surface: Dining with these companions could be a shared undertaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A joint affair' sounds like a shared venture; a joint is a cut of meat, the natural meal for this zoological order of meat-eaters.
explanation.definitionFit: The zoological order of flesh-eating mammals, such as cats, dogs and bears, which feed on meat.

clue.text: Give Heather a ring — but mind your language!

parts.note: ling is another name for common heather
the letter O is round like a ring

explanation.surface: Someone is told to phone Heather but watch their words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give Heather a ring' suggests a phone call; Heather is the plant (LING), and the ring is the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a tongue or jargon, especially one that sounds foreign or strange.

clue.text: This drop belongs to Flora

parts.note: Flora is the Roman goddess of flowers and also the plant life of a region, so the drop is the small white flower of late winter

explanation.surface: A drop of something is said to be Flora's property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop' suggests a drip and 'Flora' a woman's name; Flora means plant life, and the drop is the early white flower named after this weather.
explanation.definitionFit: The snowdrop is a plant, so its first half, the white winter weather, is the drop that belongs among the flowers.

clue.text: Band of Hope rejects?

parts.note: the Band of Hope was a temperance society for children; read literally, a band of people who reject hope are gloomy types

explanation.surface: People turned away by a temperance youth group.
explanation.walkthrough: The Band of Hope was a British temperance society for young people; read as 'a band who reject hope', it describes those who always expect the worst.
explanation.definitionFit: Habitual gloom-mongers who expect the worst, a group that turns its back on hope.
